annotation.title_clean: Guidance for Regulation of Artificial Intelligence Applications (Draft OMB Memorandum)
annotation.title_en: Guidance for Regulation of Artificial Intelligence Applications (Draft OMB Memorandum)
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Office of Management and Budget (OMB), Executive Office of the President; Vought, R.T. (Acting Director)
named_instruments_referenced: John S. McCain NDAA FY2019 Sec. 238(g)
annotation.summary_en: Draft OMB memorandum implementing Executive Order 13859 that guides US federal agencies on regulating private-sector AI applications. It sets out ten stewardship principles, including public trust, risk assessment and cost-benefit analysis. It prefers non-regulatory approaches and discourages a precautionary stance. It also includes a template for agency plans. Robots appear only in the statutory definition of AI.
key_provisions_or_claims: Agencies must avoid regulatory actions that needlessly hamper AI innovation and must avoid a precautionary approach
Ten principles for AI stewardship, including public trust, public participation, scientific integrity, and risk assessment and management
Agencies should consider non-regulatory approaches such as sector guidance, pilots and voluntary consensus standards, and rely on private-sector conformity assessment
Federal action may preempt inconsistent, burdensome state laws to support a national market
Agencies are to submit plans listing their AI statutory authorities, regulatory barriers and planned actions
